sentences.text: New rules will cover F1 races delayed or disrupted by rain or incidents from 2027 Formula 1 has announced the maximum race distance for grands prix will be reduced by 15km from 305km (189.5 miles) to 290km (180.2 miles) for the 2027 season.
sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.text: Grands prix are limited to a maximum of two hours of racing, but when there are interruptions caused by rain or accidents, a "hard stop time" will replace the current maximum three-hour duration to finish the event.
sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.text: This will allow for greater flexibility to complete disrupted races.
sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.text: A statement from governing body the FIA said: "These changes were introduced to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur." The hard stop time will vary from race to race, depending on local conditions.
sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.text: At night races, for example, there will be more flexibility to allow the race to run later than at a daytime race when there is a relatively early sunset.
sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.text: The reduction in race distance has been introduced because the ratio of internal combustion to electrical power is changing from 53-47 this year to 58-42 next year, before becoming 60-40 in 2028.
sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.text: This means that the cars will use more fuel, and that became a concern when it emerged that some teams wanted to carry their chassis over into next year to save money.
sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.article_title: F1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km

sentences.text: Jyoti and Bharat Patel are "super testers" of dementia technology in an NHS trial There are sensors in every room of Jyoti and Bharat Patel's home.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Their movements and habits are monitored constantly.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: But this doesn't worry them, in fact it gives them peace of mind.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Jyoti was diagnosed with dementia five years ago, and they are now part of an NHS trial using high-tech devices to help patients live at home safely.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: The couple, who are in their 70s, are one of more than 250 families participating in the project by the UK Dementia Research Institute (UK DRI).
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: The hope is that the technology could be extended more widely across the health service, to reduce preventable trips to hospital and give families peace of mind.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Bharat and Jyoti travelled all over the world as professional magicians Bharat and Jyoti met at a magic show in 1977 and became a double act, with their career leading them to meet King Charles and Princess Anne as well as a host of celebrities.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: In 2019, Bharat started noticing that Jyoti was making uncharacteristic mistakes on stage.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: "Normally she used to set my stage up and everything was perfect, but I saw something I was looking for and it wasn't there, so I thought something is wrong," he said.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: They went to a private health specialist who diagnosed Jyoti with Alzheimer's in 2021.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Jyoti says when she went out, if she did not look around her, she would find that she was lost.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: "I didn't know it [was] dementia but I knew it was something which [was] unusual," Bharat says.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: The couple sleep on a smart mattress that tracks Jyoti's heart rate and breathing In 2023, they were approached by the team at UK Dementia Research Institute and Imperial College London to take part in the trial, which is funded by the medical research charity LifeArc.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Their house in west London is now fitted with different sensors, which are connected via the internet, that send data back to a dedicated team of doctors, nurses and other clinical specialists.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: The team then uses the information to better understand how the person is managing their daily routine, identify early signs of changing health and care needs with the hope that they can maintain independence for longer.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Door sensors detect if someone leaves in the middle of the night, movement is monitored to check for signs of a fall, while kitchen appliances are fitted with sensors to check whether Jyoti has eaten and is sticking to her daily routine.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: The couple sleep on a "smart mattress" to track sleep disturbances and Jyoti's heart and breathing rates, which can spot early signs of an infection.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Alongside this trial, Jyoti is also testing out smart socks and a special watch that also contain sensors to monitor her body temperature and keep track of any long-term changes in her gait - indicating frailty.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Costs are expected to be about £2,000 a year, mainly to cover the monitoring and paying healthcare staff to analyse the data.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: If rolled out more widely that could be a significant amount of money with almost a million people living with dementia in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: But Sarah Daniels, health and social care lead at the UK Dementia Research Institute, says the cost is no more than a couple of weeks in a care home.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: The main aim, she says, is to give earlier signals to health and social care professionals.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: "Earlier signals means earlier intervention, which means we can head potential complications of an infection, potential challenges around care, we can head that off before it becomes a crisis," says Daniels.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Devices around the home pick up movement and alert care staff if needed None of the devices record sound or video, protecting the individual's privacy, however, some people may feel nervous about the amount of data they are allowing other people to access.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Daniels argues that by enhancing the level of information you provide to your GP, it enables them to make better decisions about your care.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: The number of people with dementia in the UK is expected to climb by another 40% by 2040, so the hope is to extend it more widely across the health service.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Dr Jeremy Isaacs, national clinical director for dementia and older people's mental health at NHS England, said the health service would be closely monitoring the trial and said the research built on NHS programmes which were already supporting people to remain more independent in their own homes.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: While some people might feel uneasy about having all these sensors in their home, Bharat says they give him greater "peace of mind".
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: "Even if it can cut down my worries by 5 or 10%, then it helps me and it will help other people too," he says.
sentences.article_title: Smart beds and motion sensors - is this the future of dementia care?

sentences.text: Specialist courts to handle cases of rape and other sexual offences will be introduced across England and Wales over the next two years, the prime minister has announced.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Each crown court will have at least one courtroom set up to hear such cases, while alleged victims will be able to view proceedings remotely and give evidence from a separate room via video link.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: They will also be provided with private entrances and waiting rooms to separate them from defendants, though this will be dependent on the architecture of each building.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Rape Crisis England and Wales said this was a "significant step forward" that would introduce several reforms it had been requesting for years.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "Taken together, they reflect the urgency of ensuring that courts are fit for purpose and properly meet the needs of victims and survivors, which is crucial to securing justice," the charity's chief executive, Ciara Bergman, said.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Charities have complained that low prosecution rates for sexual offences and delays to court proceedings had disuaded victims from coming forward or pursuing justice.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Just 2.8% of rape offences recorded by police led to prosecutions in the year ending March 2024 and were the crimes that took the longest to investigate.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: A prior ONS study, using data from 2017-2020, suggested that only a sixth of the actual number of rape and attempted rape victims had reported their assault to the police, with more than a third saying this was because they felt the police could not help or that the process would be humiliating.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Victims minister Alex Davies-Jones said the new measures were part of efforts to bring down a backlog of Crown Court cases, which stood at 80,098 at the end of March.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Rape Crisis England and Wales said 15,373 of these cases - 19% - related to sexual offences.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Davies-Jones told BBC Breakfast that the introduction of specialist courtrooms "isn't enough on its own" to tackle the backlog and stressed the importance of the Courts and Tribunals Bill to improve "timeliness, effectiveness and also prevention".
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: The Conservatives say the "long overdue" move should not come with restricting the number of jury trials, which is another provision of the bill.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Under the new measures, expected to cost around £23m of the Ministry of Justice's budget, court staff will also be given "trauma-informed training" and a single person of contact will be assigned to each survivor.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: From next month, trials will be given a fixed date rather than placed on floating lists in what Prime Minister Andy Burnham said was an effort to "rebalance the scales of justice and put victims first".
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: There are 84 crown court buildings across England and Wales, containing around 500 courtrooms, and Davies-Jones said the government was determined that every one of them would have at least one specialist rape and sexual offences courtroom by 2028.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Where architecture might prevent courtroom upgrades, Davies-Jones said staff would be expected to co-ordinate a "trauma informed approach" - for instance by scheduling different arrival times and rooms to give evidence from for victims and defendants.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: The government said the changes follow Labour MP Charlotte Nichols showing "immense strength and bravery" in speaking publicly about being raped and calling for changes to the justice system.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Nichols waived her automatic right to anonymity in March when she made a Commons speech in which she described having to wait more than 1,000 days to go to court.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Labour promised in its 2024 manifesto to halve violence against women and girls within a decade.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "For too long, victims of rape and serious sexual offences have felt let down by our justice system," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "Prosecution rates for rape remain shamefully low, with many victims waiting years for justice.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: This is not good enough." Nichols accused the then-Justice Secretary David Lammy of using victims as a "cudgel" to push through his reforms of the legal system when she spoke publicly for the first time about being raped.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: She was criticising the Courts and Tribunals Bill's plans to limit jury trials to cases with a likely prison sentence of three years or more.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Nichols said she had waited 1,088 days to go to court, with every day being "agony".
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Her attacker, she said, was acquitted at crown court but subsequently ordered to pay compensation after she won a civil case against him.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "It is because I have endured every indignity that our broken criminal justice system could mete out that I care what kind of reform will actually deliver justice for survivors and victims of crime more widely," she said.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: The Conservatives said in response to news of the specialist courts roll-out that tackling delays to criminal rape trials was "long overdue", while pushing Labour to commit to scrapping plans to restrict jury trials.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "The fact that victims have been withdrawing their cases because they have taken too long has been a disgrace," said shadow justice secretary Nick Timothy.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "Labour need to get courts sitting throughout the year, end the delays and clear the backlog – not undermine our right to a trial by jury." Last year, the Salford Survivor Project charity said victims of rape and sexual assault were being "failed by the system" as court backlogs reached a record high.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: The long delays for cases to go to trial were having a serious impact on victims' mental health, it said.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: A few months later, a woman who says she was sexually assaulted by a taxi driver on her 21st birthday told BBC News she had dropped the case because of court delays.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: She reported the alleged incident in early 2022 and gave evidence in court in December 2023, but the case was adjourned until September 2024 when the judge fell ill.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: "I couldn't let this hurt me further," she said.
sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Tory leader Kemi Badenoch (left) and shadow culture secretary Rebecca Paul visited Bicester Village, a designer outlet shopping centre popular with tourists, to promote the policy The Conservative Party has pledged to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists from outside the European Union.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: The Tories said the decision to scrap the scheme in 2021 left the UK less competitive than European destinations.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: Leader Kemi Badenoch, who was a Treasury minister when the tax relief was abolished, said businesses were being "let down by a tax policy that is chasing their customers away".
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: But Labour accused the party of "a spectacular U-turn".
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: The VAT Retail Export Scheme - which allowed overseas visitors to get a VAT refund on items they had bought in Great Britain and took home in their luggage - was scrapped for non-EU visitors under the previous Conservative government in 2021, while it was also not extended for EU visitors.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: At the time, Badenoch said it was "a costly relief which does not benefit the whole of GB equally".
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: However, the Conservatives have now set out plans to restore VAT refunds for eligible visitors from outside the EU.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: The party said that if evidence confirms the scheme "pays its way", this would be extended to visitors from the EU by the end of the next Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: It said the cost of reintroducing the scheme would be offset by cracking down on "NHS health tourism", including more consistent charging of patients ineligible for free treatment, minimum recovery targets for debts and requiring full repayment of debts before visa applications or renewals will be considered.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: The remaining costs would be funded from a package of savings set out by the Tories last year.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping, businesses say Bring back duty-free perk to boost London - mayor The party also argued the move would benefit shops, hotels, restaurants and the wider tourism industry.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: It pointed to research by the Centre for Economics and Business Research (Cebr), which suggested fully restoring tax-free shopping for tourists could attract up to 2.35 million extra visitors and generate £4.1bn in extra spending.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: The report from earlier this month also estimated that for every £1 of VAT refunded, this could generate £1.54 in other taxes.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: Badenoch said: "We have iconic retailers, inventive designers and brilliant manufacturers, but they are being let down by a tax policy that is chasing their customers away.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: "Holidaymakers are choosing rival cities in other countries for the simple reason that it saves them money." Businesses have long called for tax-free shopping for tourists to be reintroduced, arguing they are at a disadvantage to other European countries.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: EU countries offer VAT refunds for non-EU visitors, while other European countries such as Switzerland have similar schemes.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: Helen Dickinson, chief executive at the British Retail Consortium, said: "Introducing a modern tax-free shopping scheme would help attract more international spending to the UK, supporting high streets, jobs and investment in towns and cities across the country.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: "Done properly, it would boost economic growth and deliver a net benefit to the Exchequer." However, a Labour spokesperson said: "Kemi Badenoch used to say tax-free shopping was a costly giveaway and now she's trying to sell it as an economic miracle.
sentences.article_title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists

sentences.text: "If they really think it's such a great idea, they should explain why they scrapped it in the first place and how they'd pay for bringing it back." Sign up for our Politics Essential newsletter to keep up with the inner workings of Westminster and beyond.

sentences.text: Scotland's 32 councils could be replaced by as few as six regional authorities, the government has suggested.

sentences.article_title: Scotland's 32 councils could be cut to six under government plan

sentences.text: "If the defendant has any sense of decency at all, he will carry the weight of what he did until the end of his days," he said.

sentences.text: Judge Mills said it was "simply by chance" that "more people were not killed" as a result of his "dangerous" and "completely selfish actions".
sentences.article_title: Driver jailed after killing 'devoted' mum while fleeing police

sentences.text: Flights in Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England have been affected by air traffic control issues – the second major disruption at UK airports in a few weeks.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: When a flight is cancelled or delayed, passengers affected have various rights, such as a refund or an alternative flight at no extra cost.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: However, these can vary depending on which carrier you are flying with and from where.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Extra compensation is payable only when an airline is at fault, which is not the case with air traffic control problems.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Here's what it means for you.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Under UK law, airlines have a duty to look after you when flights are delayed or cancelled.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: The reason for the delay or cancellation does not matter.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: So anyone affected by the air transport delays will be eligible.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: That includes providing meals and accommodation, if necessary, and getting you to your destination.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: The airline should organise putting you on an alternative flight at no extra cost.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Additional losses, such as unused accommodation, might require a claim to a credit card provider, if that was the payment option used.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Passengers are also being urged to heed travel advice from the UK government , external , as this can also affect travel insurance rights.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: UK law generally applies to your flight if you are flying from a UK airport on any airline, arriving at a UK airport on an EU or UK airline, or arriving at an airport in the EU on a UK airline.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If your flight was coming into the UK on a non-UK or EU airline, then you should check the terms and conditions of your booking.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If your flight is covered by UK law, your airline must let you choose between either getting a refund or being booked on to an alternative flight.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: That's regardless of how far in advance the cancellation was made.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: You can get your money back for any part of the ticket you have not used.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: So, if you booked a return flight and the outbound leg is cancelled, you can get the full cost of the return ticket refunded.

sentences.text: This video can not be played Freddo the robot in action at Vsim Freddo the robot walks across the office and takes a plastic bottle offered by a staff member.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Given that a robot recently beat Usain Bolt's 100m sprint record, it's not the most startling achievement.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But the speed by which Freddo has been trained to walk, recognise the bottle and grasp it is impressive.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It took just a few minutes to develop those skills and upload them to Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: His developers say rival systems could take days to attain such skills.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: I'm at Vsim, a British start-up based in Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey hope one day their software will control robots that can navigate and do useful tasks in the home and workplace.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It's a weird situation with robotics because actually the stuff that we find as humans to be incredibly difficult, like gymnastics, you can get robots to do reasonably well.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The stuff that humans are really good at, like fine dexterity, is really hard in robots," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Vsim founders Michelle Lu and Kier Storey Freddo's skills were honed in a virtual environment, where a task can be performed  in a computer simulation millions of times.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Such virtual simulations are a common way to train robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Tech giant Nvidia has a system called Isaac Sim which works that way - Lu and Storey both worked on an early version of it.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: In 2022 they decided to set up Vsim, to build the their own training system environment and other tools.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "The underlying algorithms that we were using for most of these robotic simulations they hark back to the 1970s and 1980s, but those algorithms are not really brilliant fits for GPUs," Storey says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Within months they realised their system could work much faster than anything they had seen before.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Eighteen months in and we actually have a completely functional, super high-performance simulator," says Lu.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The software is so efficient that it can run on the hardware carried by Freddo.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That means the robot can run tens of thousand of simulations while it is moving around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It can look about a second, or so, ahead into the future for 20,000 different kind of combinations of things that might happen," Storey explains.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And that would be vital for a robot moving around an unstructured environment like the average home.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Things outside of the robot's control, like humans, animals or even other robots, could do things that require a change of strategy.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Robot training systems use virtual environments where tasks are practised Vsim is a start-up with 10 engineers working on its tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: The problem is when you start doing long-horizon tasks, where I say: 'I want you to take the bottle and I want you to fill it up and I want you to go pour'," says Spencer Huang, director of product for robotics at Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: This year Nvidia has started using AI agents to help build virtual environments to train robots and validate whether the solutions from training work or not.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: They can also be trained by watching human or video demonstrations.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says their system has "reduced approximation, using accurate simulations to train models that genuinely work in reality as well as they do in simulations." Soon a second robot, to be called Nacho, will be helping develop that tech.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Lu says that should speed up their development process and ensure their software can run on different machines.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: And, of course, provide Freddo with some company.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Health spokesperson Helen Morgan met parents and babies to discuss maternity care Liberal Democrats are calling for one-to-one midwife care for women in labour, as figures suggest life-altering childbirth injuries in England have reached record levels.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Lib Dem analysis of NHS figures showed the number of women suffering potentially life-threatening levels of blood loss is the highest ever recorded in England.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Three in every 100 women suffered serious tearing injuries requiring emergency surgery in the first half of this year, something party leader Sir Ed Davey said was a "devastating indictment of our NHS maternity services".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The government is expected to publish a new national maternity and neonatal action plan by the end of the year.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: He said £1.3bn a year was currently being spent on "failure" through negligence compensation payouts for poor maternity services, but said this investment should go towards prevention instead.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Calling for more senior midwives and consultants, he said: "Our current maternity staff are run ragged - they're massively overstretched.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "That's the best way, all the evidence shows, to make sure maternity units are safe," he added.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "It is a scandal at the moment - we've seen inquiry after inquiry.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: So many women are suffering injuries at birth and we're seeing the loss of babies too; it is a tragedy as well as a scandal." He said ministers "cannot turn a blind eye to this national safety scandal" and mothers "deserve safe, compassionate care".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The Lib Dems are calling for a consultant obstetrician to be present on every labour ward at all hours, one-to-one midwifery care for every woman in labour, and recruit an extra 300 consultant midwives.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The party pointed to Care Quality Commission (CQC) survey data showing one-in-10 women, about 54,000, were left alone during late stages of labour or childbirth last year, which the Lib Dems said was due to lack of training and staff shortages.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: More than 8,000 women had postpartum haemorrhages with blood loss of more than 1.5l since the start of this year, more than double the number over the equivalent period in 2021, the party's analysis of NHS figures suggests.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Rates of major haemorrhage peaked between April and June this year, while 32.7 women per thousand needed emergency treatment.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The rate of third or fourth degree vaginal tears during childbirth has risen by 29% in the last five years, according to the analysis.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The Lib Dem health spokesperson Helen Morgan, who successfully campaigned for an independent maternity commissioner to drive improvements, said reports on previous maternity scandals were "gathering dust".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "Years after the Shrewsbury and Telford scandal which devastated my community - my neighbours and friends - women continue to suffer," she said.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "This must be the moment we say 'enough'." A review in 2022 found catastrophic failures at Shrewsbury and Telford NHS Trust (SaTH) over 20 years may have led to the deaths of more than 200 babies.

sentences.text: "Every woman deserves safe maternity care and the new health secretary has made this issue a personal priority," they said.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: This video can not be played Ed Davey says the Lib Dems have "a historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform" Sir Ed Davey said the Liberal Democrats are "a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform" as the party's conference began in Brighton.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: The Lib Dem leader sought to strike a combative stance as he faced down some criticism from MPs, including one who said publicly that they felt the party was struggling for relevance.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: On the first day of the autumn conference, Sir Ed warned an "unholy alliance" between Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch and Farage could turn the UK into a "Trump satellite state".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Addressing speculation about a possible snap election, he said the party was ready to fight and would build its so-called orange wall even higher by winning more than its 2024 record of 72 MPs.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Sir Ed's attention-grabbing stunts helped raise the party's profile ahead of the last election, but recent polling showed 43% of respondents were unclear what the Liberal Democrats stand for, with just over half describing them as "weak".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Asked about her comments, Sir Ed said: "No, I heard Roz [Savage], and I really value her, but I think she's wrong on that.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "If you look at our election results up and down the country, we now run more councils than the Conservatives." He added: "Listen, MPs get elected and they get frustrated because they can't change the world.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "I'm afraid that's the political system.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: I've been used to it for a little while and people are learning about that frustration." Speaking on the pebbles of Brighton Beach, Sir Ed told reporters the Liberal Democrats would fight to stop a Reform government.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "One of the things that makes us unique is that we are a firewall against Nigel Farage and Reform," he said.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "Many of the seats he needs to get himself into No 10 are seats that we will defend and indeed win - and we are also able to take seats off the Conservatives, because I really fear that Kemi Badenoch will give the keys to No 10 to Nigel Farage, so we have got to stop the Conservatives as well.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "We have got an historic opportunity to win many more seats and a moral responsibility to stop Reform." He added a manifesto working group had already been set up in case of an early election "so we'll be ready if it comes early, but, you know, it still could be up to three years away".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Sir Ed insisted his party has a "distinctive position" in British politics, and will use the four-day conference to position it to take on the challenge from Reform as well as its typical rivals the Conservatives, talking up their focus on the NHS and goal of re-joining the EU single market and customs union.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: The Lib Dem leader highlighted how six former Conservative cabinet ministers were among 25 Tories to have defected to Reform in the last two years, claiming they were now competing with each other to see who can divide the country more, rather than looking to fix the country's problems.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "An unholy alliance between Farage and Badenoch is the only way either can get into power," he said.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "Together, they want to turn Britain into a Trump satellite state which would trash our NHS, turn our communities against each other, cause untold damage to our environment, and trample over traditional British values of fairness, tolerance, and decency.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: "A bigger Orange Wall is the only thing that can stand between Britain and this dangerous experiment, and we will not let them pass." Davey also attacked the Labour government as having no plan for growth, failing to support families struggling with the cost of living and taxing small businesses "to the brink".
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Ahead of a speech to party members, Davey urged Liberal Democrats not to look away from injustice or "human dignity under attack" but to fight back.
sentences.article_title: Davey says Lib Dems are 'firewall against Farage' as conference begins

sentences.text: Harrogate and Knaresborough Lib Dem MP Tom Gordon would like to see devolution go further A Liberal Democrat MP has called on Prime Minister Andy Burnham to go further with his devolution plans and give Yorkshire its own parliament.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Harrogate and Knaresborough MP Tom Gordon said too much power was currently in the hands of elected mayors and a Yorkshire parliament would better reflect the region.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Burnham has recently set out plans to give elected mayors more power over planning and tackling fly-tipping and said he would give them a share of income tax and business rates.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: But Gordon told BBC Politics North he believed that giving more money and powers to four separate Yorkshire mayoralties actually deepened divides in the county and a Yorkshire parliament would be "a good thing".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Yorkshire currently has three Labour mayors - Oliver Coppard for South Yorkshire, Tracy Brabin for West Yorkshire and David Skaith for York and North Yorkshire - as well as Luke Campbell, the Reform UK mayor of Hull and East Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: The Lib Dem said that while people had been told the recent local government reorganisation in North Yorkshire would "simplify" the situation, he believed that was not the case.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "We've ended up with a new North Yorkshire Council at a higher tier and a Harrogate town council below it, so we've ended up with two tiers.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: In fact, there's a third tier when you throw in the regional mayor," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "So we've ended up with more tiers, but those powers have been moved upwards rather than down to people.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "I think we owe it to have everyone have a seat at that table, not just all that power put in one person's hands." Gordon said he believed a Yorkshire parliament was the way forward "if it's good enough for Scotland, if it's good enough for Wales, if it's good enough for London".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "We should have a model where we have broader people elected to it who can feed in all those issues into a Yorkshire-wide parliament.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: That, to me, is only a good thing," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: The idea of a Yorkshire parliament has previously been advocated by the Yorkshire Party.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Since 2014, the party has argued that it would create a more "engaged, democratic society".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Meanwhile, when devolution deals were first being discussed, a proposal was put forward for one mayor for all of Yorkshire.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: The so-called "One Yorkshire" plan was backed by 18 of the region's 20 local councils, while Sheffield and Rotherham opted for a separate South Yorkshire solution.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: However, the then Conservative Communities Secretary James Brokenshire rejected the proposal and said the plan did "not meet our criteria" .
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Deals were later done for the four counties within Yorkshire In a speech earlier this year, Burnham said decision-making needed to be "pushed to regions and local communities" , adding that it would see "good growth in every postcode".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: David Skaith says Yorkshire's mayors work "collectively" Responding to Gordon's comments, Skaith said the Greater Manchester and Liverpool City Region, which has had devolved powers for longer, had worked "really well".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: But Skaith also said he believed that all views were represented within the current system.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "It's not just four mayors who sit in Yorkshire, all our combined authorities are made up of those local authorities as well," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "So, I'm not making decisions sat in York and North Yorkshire on my own.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: It's in partnership with the two local authorities." Skaith pointed to the so-called "White Rose Agreement", signed by himself and the mayors of South and West Yorkshire, pledging to work closer on things like transport.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: “Rail is a classic case - Northern Powerhouse Rail - where we got particularly the working around York station and the wider area of North Yorkshire," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "We have got that collective buy-in as to what we want for Yorkshire for rail.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "That's why we've got so far with government, because we work collectively as mayors, because we know our transport is so interconnected." When he was prime minister, David Cameron, together with Chancellor George Osborne, previously introduced "devolution deals".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Successive Conservative governments have extended those deals and powers for regional mayors.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: However, York Conservative councillor Chris Steward warned that a parliament for Yorkshire would be "an absurd, costly and bureaucratic nonsense".
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "I am a proud Yorkshireman, having lived here all my life," he said.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "But while it is a county for so much - from the scenery to county cricket to all the things making it famous - as we saw in the discussions about devolution, it is not a functional economic geography and politics viewed across the region would not work.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: "People do not want yet another layer of politicians and the related expenses." Reform UK has been approached for comment.
sentences.article_title: MP calls for Yorkshire to get its own parliament

sentences.text: Eric Fawley said he had been drawing since he was five years old A 94-year-old man with dementia said he was "very happy" to be given the opportunity to have his artwork exhibited in the House of Commons.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Eric Fawley, from Blackpool, has produced hundreds of drawings since arriving at Greenbanks Care Home in Watford, Hertfordshire, over a year ago, after a fire at his home.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: His drawings and paintings depict the world around him, as well as his former bosses at BT.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: The exhibition was facilitated by the Watford Labour MP Matt Turmaine after he saw Fawley's work at the care home.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: This is one of the few drawings Fawley has produced in colour, as he prefers to sketch in black and white Fawley said he began creating artworks from an early age, encouraged by his mother, a violinist, and his father, a gifted amateur painter.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: His family were unable to support his ambition to attend art school.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: He left school at the age of 14 and worked in a variety of jobs, including electrical work for the famous Blackpool illuminations, before going on to become a Post Office engineer with BT.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: When drawing someone, he said it was important to start with their hair.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: "If the hair is wrong, then everything is wrong," he added.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Fawley's sketches of former colleagues at BT won him several art competitions.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: One of Fawley's wartime sketches features his sister, Charlotte, who regularly visits him at the care home Since moving to Greenbanks in March last year, Fawley has continued to sketch.

sentences.text: He said being creative helped to focus his mind and "ensures that every day is different".
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: He has held exhibitions across Essex and also performed a ceremonial ribbon-cutting at an exhibition at Harlow Library.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Staff at the care home are "super proud of him" and are "excited" to see his artwork gain wider recognition, with Fawley challenging perceptions of what people can achieve in care.

sentences.text: Burnham said it "feels very fitting" to welcome Martin as the first international visitor to Number 10 North Ireland's relationship with the UK under Andy Burnham's premiership has got off to a "very good start", Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin has said.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: But he refused to be drawn on how much the issue of Irish unity had featured during their first official meeting at Number 10 North on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The visit came days after US President Donald Trump made comments about supporting a "unified Ireland".
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Martin said the men had a "broad discussion" about upholding the Good Friday Agreement and that they did not get into specifics.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: "It was the first meeting, it went well...
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: I think we have the capacity to make a lot of progress on a lot of issues in the time ahead," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Martin was the first international leader to visit the government's new headquarters in Manchester, and also visited the Brian Boru Irish Club in Burnham's constituency in Ashton-in-Makerfield.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: On his visit to Northern Ireland last month, Burnham said a border poll was " off the table ", but later said he stood by the Good Friday Agreement.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The taoiseach and prime minister visited the Brian Boru Irish Club in Ashton-in-Makerfield The taoiseach said he and the prime minister had discussed the UK's Troubles legacy legislation in depth, and that he had "stressed the importance" of passing the bill through Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The government is expected to publish details of changes in the middle of next month, with Martin saying both London and Dublin had been working closely on it.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: He also said both he and the prime minister wanted to see the power-sharing institutions at Stormont working more effectively, and that the Irish government believes there needs to be reform.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: He said Burnham understood the issue and was currently focused on trying to resolve negotiations with the Stormont executive to agree a budget for this year.

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Former consultant hopes Letby inquiry recommendations will prevent deaths happening again One of the senior doctors who tried to raise concerns about Lucy Letby with hospital managers has told the BBC the final inquiry report makes for "grim reading".

sentences.text: Consultant paediatrician Dr John Gibbs worked at the Countess of Chester Hospital throughout the period in 2015 to 2016 when Letby murdered seven babies, and attempted to murder seven more, on the neonatal unit.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "I wish we consultants had been brave enough to follow our suspicions and escalate things to the police earlier," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "When I say, 'we consultants', I am responsible as well and if my other consultant colleagues didn't go to the police, I should have." The Thirlwall Inquiry was launched after former nurse Letby was convicted in 2023, and the final report was published on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: In the 822-page document, Lady Justice Thirlwall described "a complete failure to protect babies on the neonatal unit at the Countess of Chester Hospital".
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The report found that the police "should have been notified earlier than they were" and that hospital managers had repeatedly dismissed consultants' concerns.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Reflecting on the findings for the first time, Gibbs said: "I wasn't expecting it to be an easy read and it certainly isn't.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: I'd imagine it's an extremely difficult read for the parents of the babies concerned.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "But it was during that 11 months after Lucy Letby was moved off the unit, before the police got involved, that it was a very difficult atmosphere, very tense, very stressful dealing with the managers," he added.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Managers "were determined to ensure that we accepted Lucy Letby had been wrongly suspected of doing any harm," the senior doctor explained.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He also spoke of the failures of his and his wider team, specifically referencing a doctor who disregarded blood test results that suggested a baby had been poisoned with insulin in August 2015.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: While one of his colleagues had missed the relevance of the results when they came back from the lab, it had been a collective team failure, Dr Gibbs concluded.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: "Others of us were on call and covering the neonatal unit over the next week or two before the baby moved out of the unit.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: We all had the opportunity to review the notes." Letby, who maintains her innocence, is serving 15 whole-life terms for the murders and has twice been denied permission to appeal against her convictions.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The Criminal Cases Review Commission (CCRC), an independent body set up to examine potential miscarriages of justice, is currently reviewing her convictions.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: The inquiry looked into the actions of managers at the hospital where Lucy Letby worked In the weeks and months after Letby was convicted, questions about the case arose in the form of online conspiracy theories and discourse from serious academics, including medical experts and statisticians.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: Gibbs said that the continuing support for Letby had taken a toll on him and other consultants, and that claims she had been wrongly convicted were "frustrating and difficult" to hear.
sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.article_title: Letby doctor says inquiry 'grim reading' and he wishes 'we had been brave enough to follow suspicions'

sentences.text: He added: "I haven't changed my mind that I think Lucy Letby is guilty." However, he emphasised that, because of the "calibre of some of the people who've raised concerns", it is "important" that the evidence used to convict Letby is being examined by the CCRC.
