sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The research has raised questions about what it means to alter the way laboratory  animals think and feel Neuroscientists in the US have successfully adapted mice to have functioning human cells inside their own brains.

sentences.article_title: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough

sentences.article_title: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough

sentences.text: Some conditions cannot be studied in a mouse, simply because rodents do not develop some of the brain disorders that we do.
sentences.article_title: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough

sentences.text: As lead researcher Prof Sergiu Pașca from Stanford University explained in a press conference, psychiatry has "one of the lowest success rates for clinical trials".
sentences.article_title: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough

sentences.article_title: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough

sentences.text: "That tells us we're missing a lot of information about human biology and capturing that will be essential." The Stanford researchers said that, for some complex conditions, including epilepsy, autism and cerebral palsy, it has the potential to be "transformative".

sentences.text: While this research is not the first time human neurons have been implanted in laboratory rodents , external , these scientists took that approach to a new level.
sentences.article_title: Part-human part-mouse brain developed in science breakthrough

sentences.text: The BBC's defence correspondent explains what the US announcement means The announcement by the United States that it has deployed a space weapon in Earth's orbit has raised questions about what weaponry is actually in space, and what role it could play in efforts by great powers to dominate that arena.

sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Space has been a militarised domain since the start of the space age - in the late 1960s, the Soviet Union deployed weapons up there.

sentences.text: The Istrebitel Sputnikov (IS; Satellite Destroyer) programme was made up of satellites that were designed to release projectiles that detonated, releasing shrapnel into the path of another (usually American) satellite.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Nowadays, advanced militaries deploy satellites in space for a range of purposes, including reconnaissance, secure communications, detecting missile launches and providing precise location information for targeted strikes.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: As warfare becomes more technologically advanced, analysts expect the use of military hardware in space to increase.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Some types of space weaponry could create a lot of debris and destruction Dr Bleddyn Bowen, an associate fellow in military sciences at the Royal United Services Institute and associate professor in astropolitics at Durham University, said he was only able to hazard a guess about the weapon announced by the US.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "I would expect there to be some kind of electronic warfare or radio-jamming platform, possibly, this would be a non-destructive kind of anti-satellite weapon," he told BBC Radio 4's Today programme.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Such weaponry already exists on Earth and can disrupt satellite communications, he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "If you take out the radio links then your satellite is very useless." Bowen also would not rule out a riskier and more disruptive type of weaponry, which could create debris and destruction.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "Less likely would be a kinetic kill vehicle of some sort, so a vehicle that would release a projectile that could ram into a satellite and destroy it," he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: A type of "close inspection and grappling satellite would be another possibility as well." As to whether rivals such as Russia and China have similar weaponry already in orbit, is difficult to tell.

sentences.text: "If we're looking towards China and Russia, they have both displayed activity," Juliana Suess, a former research fellow at RUSI and researcher at the Stiftung Wissenschaft und Politik (German Institute for International and Security Affairs), told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "For example, with Russia, we've seen some activity that hints at being a co-orbital weapons test.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: So we saw something that might indicate that they shot a projectile as a test in orbit.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: In a later BBC interview, Bowen was dismissive of China's reaction to the US announcement which warned against an arms race in space, describing it as "the pot calling the kettle black".
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "If you're already an expert... you know how hollow those words are coming from the Russian and Chinese governments," he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "The United States, Russia and China and also India have all developed different kinds of anti-satellite or counter-space weapons, and Russia and China have put a lot of technologies in space which have a lot of weapons potential," he added.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: In fact in the past 10 years, Russia and China have been doing a lot more manoeuvres in space, known as rendezvous and proximity operations (RPOs) - "buzzing" Western satellites.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "Theoretically, these RPO [satellites]can become hunter-killer satellites by physically colliding with them or by nudging them out of orbit," Dr Rod Thornton, reader in Russian Defence and Security Studies at King's College, London, told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Bowen added that the Chinese have demonstrated "space tug capability", saying: "A vehicle can go up to a satellite, can grapple it and move it into a different orbit." sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: However, some types of space weaponry also have the potential to create huge amounts of space junk.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: "It doesn't have to be a sort of huge piece of metal to do any damage, it can be a tiny piece of plastic, given the velocity that we're talking about in orbit," she said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: They also have ASAT [air-launched antisatellite] missiles that can be launched from a great height by aircraft," he said.
sentences.article_title: What weapon could the US have put into space?

sentences.text: Only if it was happening on the ground as well.

sentences.text: "What could happen in space is not something that would happen in isolation, really," Bowen said.

sentences.text: Professor Dave Chadwick from Bangor University sampling damaged remains following wildfires at Mynydd Llangynidr in Bannau Brycheiniog Scientists investigating the damage caused by severe wildfires across Wales this summer say the impact has been "catastrophic".

sentences.text: Extreme heat and exceptionally dry conditions throughout July and August left landscapes such as heathland, moorland and upland grasslands vulnerable to fast spreading fires, resulting in one of the UK's worst wildfire seasons in recent years.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones, who is leading a Bangor University survey of several sites across Wales, said the scale of damage was far greater than what was immediately visible.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "People see the blackened vegetation and assume that's the main impact, but the real story is below our feet," said Jones.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: During the July peak, fires affected approximately 2,760 acres of countryside across north Wales alone, the equivalent of more than 1,500 football pitches.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: At Sychnant Pass in Conwy county, one of the most significant blazes saw 36 homes having to be evacuated and about 200 acres of land affected.
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: Prof Davey Jones said the scale of damage from the wildfires was far greater than what was immediately visible At Sychnant Pass today, there are slight green shoots of recovery visible among the charred hillside.

sentences.text: But Jones described a rare ecosystem housing specialist plants, butterflies and insects, "where the UK is the epicentre globally".
sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "We've probably lost about 10 centimetres of soil here [at Sychnant Pass] so we've lost all of that organic matter layer... 4,000 years of carbon gone in a single event," he said.

sentences.text: "Once the topsoil is gone, we can never recover that.

sentences.text: "This soil acts as a water sponge, a carbon store, a nutrient bank.

sentences.text: "Losing it is a double whammy, it worsens climate change and makes the habitat far more fragile." He added: "This site has taken thousands of years to develop and it's all gone in maybe five days?

sentences.text: "If we are going to try and put that soil back, generate artificial soils through the reuse of organic wastes for example, then it's important we understand what the soil quality is now.

sentences.text: "So that we can prepare for the future and design those soils, because they don't exist yet." Over recent weeks the Bangor team has been racing to collect soil samples at several sites across Wales before heavy winter rainfall washes away the remains.

sentences.article_title: Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn

sentences.text: "It was really important that we got on site very quickly to measure the soil and vegetation properties while the fire's impacts were still fresh," she said.

sentences.text: King Charles has warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He made the comments at a summit he had convened at Dumfries House in Ayrshire to discuss how the tech can be used to benefit society.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Those gathered at the meeting also included Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI Minister, the Pope's advisor, and participants from AI giants such as Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: It comes amid a series of recent warnings from people inside the industry about the rapidly evolving capabilities of advanced or "frontier" AI models and the regulation needed to keep them in check.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "Those who have created these technologies are now increasingly warning that AI risks developing darker capacities - perhaps even to take life," the King told the executives.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He said there seemed to be an "urgency" in "adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands, and being used in potentially catastrophic ways".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world," he told the group.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: The summit has been called to consider whether a "shared set of principles" can be developed to "help guide the future application" of AI.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, was among top industry leaders attending.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, supplying chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: It is also the world's most valuable company, with a stock market value of around $5.15tn.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Huang told the room he believed safety was "paramount", adding that companies should hold back a product and "keep engineering" if it was not safe enough.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: The Nvidia boss also highlighted the value of open models - systems which give users direct access to the software - as a way to "ensure that people and countries are not left behind".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He said these systems must also be protected so "researchers, universities, start-ups and countries" can develop applications "none of us would have imagined alone".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "Let us lead with responsible optimism, build AI safely and securely, open it to more people, expand our ambition and solve the problems that matter to the world," Huang added.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Meanwhile Sir Demis Hassabis, who co-founded the UK AI lab DeepMind - later acquired by Google - offered a more cautious view on the pace of development.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He said artificial general intelligence - systems it is believed could be as good as or better than humans at multiple tasks - was "probably only a few short years away" and could have an impact "ten times that of the Industrial Revolution".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: The chance of something going wrong was "definitely non-zero", Sir Demis added.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: But he advocated for "a sensible middle way", saying humanity could address risks if collectively given the space and time to mitigate them.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "The future is not yet written," he told the King's delegates.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Sarah Friar, OpenAI's chief financial officer, said AI had the potential to solve some of society's "hardest problems" - but agreed its growing capabilities raised questions about safety and "how we ensure it always serves people".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "We need to address those questions together," she said.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "No one company or government can do that alone and I'm grateful to His Majesty for convening this discussion at such an important moment." sentences.text: "Encouraging and condoning the objectification of women and the creation of explicit content from people's images has the potential to cause real-world harm." sentences.text: Patrick Hillman, the chief operating officer of Logical Intelligence, which is chaired by Yann LeCun, a sage of the AI industry, noted Tuesday how little faith people have in tech companies to do anything truly in the public interest , external .
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: "The only institution that Americans might trust less than Washington these days is Silicon Valley.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: I have worked and lived in both and I assure you both have earned this scepticism," Hillman said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: "If you believe what you are building is dangerous, show us what you are prepared to stop doing," he added.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC AI regulation faces political deadlock as calls grow for Congress to act Leaders of OpenAI and Anthropic have said they have recently started working towards some sort of industry-wide agreement on safety.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: Amodei, during a cameo at the conference on Tuesday, said Anthropic is now in "a dialogue with the rest of the industry" about committing to better safety standards and checks on AI tools and development.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: He also said that one of the biggest surprises of the AI boom was not how the technology itself has advanced, but its broader impact.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: "We didn't appreciate that it would lead to companies growing so fast, and how quickly they would become central to things," Amodei said.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: OpenAI executive Chris Lehane said last week that the company was also working with other AI labs , external "to advance frontier AI standards, building a voluntary effort now, with or without government support." Those labs include Anthropic and Google Deepmind.
sentences.article_title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms

sentences.text: "With stakes this high, we cannot let the perfect become the enemy of the good," Lehane wrote.

sentences.text: Alcohol buyers will be able to use a digital ID app on their phones to prove their age under new rules introduced on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Pubs and shops in England and Wales can use the tech in addition to current physical forms of ID - with the government saying a digital option will make age-checks quicker and more secure for customers and staff.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Customers will be able to choose ID apps from a range of suppliers such as the Post Office, Yoti or Luciditi, provided they are on a government-approved list.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The change means businesses will no longer be required to let people use physical ID, but the government contends most establishments would.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The plan will be technology-agnostic, meaning that the government is not setting out in detail how each app must work.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: It argues that under the voluntary digital ID scheme, drinkers would share fewer personal details with a venue or shop - such as tapping their phone on a reader or displaying a scannable QR code rather than handing over an official document.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The apps will also need to guard against customers borrowing devices from older friends and relatives, and ensure the ID app belongs to the person using it.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Yoti's digital ID app, for example, will only let a user log in if a scan of their face matches that of the person who signed up for the app.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The app then generates a QR code that can be scanned by a business with a free checker app, which tells them the person's age.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This is time-limited to make duping or sharing the QR code more difficult.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Digital government minister Stephanie Peacock said having the option for digital ID would "mean you do not need to carry a physical ID, nor hand over sensitive personal information" meaning people could "feel safer on a night out'".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Allen Simpson, chief executive of trade body UKHospitality, said the new rules were a "positive step".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: He added the industry would work with government to make sure the scheme's roll-out would not be "burdensome" for the hospitality sector.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This would include ensuring there were multiple options for suppliers and that it was cost-efficient, Simpson said.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The government wants digital ID apps under its scheme to work together so customers do not need to use different apps in different venues.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: It also wants the services to work offline and accessible even without mobile data or a Wi-Fi connection.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: In future, the digital proof of age scheme could be extended to cover tobacco and vapes.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: But digital rights campaigners have said such measures could lead to the exclusion of some groups.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: Jasleen Chaggar of Big Brother Watch said while having multiple ways to prove your identity was helpful, the Government should ensure that digital ID did not become effectively mandatory "as it would shut out millions of people".
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: "Many people have legitimate reasons for relying on physical ID, whether out of choice, privacy and security concerns, or because they lack the digital skills or means to use digital ID," she said.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: "The Government should expressly prohibit businesses from requiring digital IDs for age checks without offering reasonable alternatives," she added.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: The new rules come after a wider digital ID programme promoted by former Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer proved controversial , and was later abandoned by Andy Burnham.
sentences.article_title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: BBC’s Tom Gerken gets his hands on Valve's Steam Frame Valve's new virtual reality headset, the Steam Frame, has officially been released - but it comes at a high price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The hardware is excellent - a light device which feels comfortable to wear and is packed with clever technology - so long as you're willing to pay a whopping £1,089 for a headset with 1TB of storage.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The variant with 256GB of storage, meanwhile, costs £889.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Both are capable of streaming from a PC as well as playing games on-device, with varying degrees of success.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But it carries a price tag which will make a lot of people roll their eyes, and doesn't do much to dispel criticism that increasingly-costly VR headsets are pricing people out of the hobby.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But before we get into that hefty price tag, is the Steam Frame actually any good?
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: I've owned VR headsets for well over a decade, and Valve's latest effort makes a promising first impression.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Games run well - really the bare minimum considering the price tag - and it's easy enough to use.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Puzzle games like the VR version of Escape Simulator - which tasks you with solving puzzles to exit a room - run great, as you would hope One of the nice things is, like Meta's Quest 3, it has flat "pancake" lenses allowing you to see clearly when you put the headset on.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: It's light - weighing little more than a can of soup.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But what makes it comfortable is the decision to separate the internals up.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The battery pack rests on the back of your head while the screen is at the front - meaning you don't feel front-heavy, a common criticism of other headsets.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But there are better screens out there.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The PlayStation VR2 for example has incredible OLED displays, albeit without the pancake lenses.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Apple and Samsung both have excellent screens too in their own headsets.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Yet these come at a serious premium, costing significantly more than the Steam Frame.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Moss sees you guide a mouse through a series of environments which look excellent in a VR headset - even if a flat screenshot doesn't quite do it justice When Meta launched the Quest 3 in June 2023, its 128GB model retailed for £480.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Less storage, but a much lower price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Three years later, it's hard to believe VR just keeps getting more expensive when the Quest 3 felt like a turning point.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "VR today is ultimately a high-end niche," gaming writer Christopher Dring told me.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "Meta had been subsidising the Quest hardware, and it's difficult to imagine they will going forward as they pivot away from those experiences." Of course, there are reasons for prices going up.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: AI developers are building giant data centres filled with racks of powerful servers, using many of the same components needed to make devices like the Steam Frame.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Ram prices alone more than doubled in price between October 2025 and the start of 2026 .
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Meanwhile, the graphics card I bought for £500 a few months ago now sits at closer to £650.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: As prices climb higher and higher, hardware developers don't have much of a choice but to put up their own.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "We set out to come out with a device that would have been much more affordable," Valve developer Jeremy Selan said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "But the global Ram market has impacted us the same way it's impacted everybody." Selan said the firm "fought hard to get it even to this price" and made the decision to ship the Steam Frame despite the price tag The Steam Frame is certainly not a budget product.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But not everyone agrees with the suggestion that VR in general costs too much.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "The idea that it's too expensive is one of the biggest misconceptions about VR," UploadVR website editor David Heaney told me.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: He pointed out while some headsets may be expensive, Meta's Quest 3S budget model costs £320 but has been on sale for £250 several times.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "In context, a Nintendo Switch 2 is £420, an Xbox Series S is £430, and a PS5 is £470 - Quest 3S, which is primarily used for gaming, is cheaper than other games consoles," he said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: He said the big barrier to more people getting into VR was simply that "we're still in the early days".
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "You have to see VR in the same timeframe you'd see personal computers in the 1980s," he said.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "Even if they had been cheap, which they weren't, they weren't yet good enough for mainstream adoption.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: "VR is only just getting started, a tech in its 1980s PC era, not something anywhere near maturity." What makes the Steam Frame really stand out is its new tech, including what developers call its "foveated streaming".
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The tech displays only the exact thing you're looking at in the highest quality, while making things in your peripheral vision less clear.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: You don't notice the low quality bits because you're not looking at them - saving a massive amount of bandwidth.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: It means you can stream VR games wirelessly from your PC in high quality without being tethered by a cable, and it works well.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: And it does this while sending two signals at once - combining your household Wi-Fi with a dongle which plugs into your PC.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Valve's Half-Life: Alyx is the most visually stunning game I have played in VR - I've played wireless VR before, but never at this graphical quality when streaming But then again, you need to spend even more money on a decent PC if you want to benefit from that - which doesn't help with concerns about price.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Valve says despite it being a VR headset, the Steam Frame is not just for VR games.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: Selan told me the hope is people will also use it to play their non-VR games too, using the headset as a screen.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: But it's an interesting thought - and I'd love to be proven wrong.
sentences.article_title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Aliko Dangote wanted all Nigerians to get involved in the share offer Every Nigerian is now an oil magnate.

sentences.text: At least that is what the social media memes would have you believe as investor fever hits the country.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: Nigerians have been eager to have a piece of the energy business that was built up by the country's – and continent's – richest man: Aliko Dangote.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: More than four billion shares in his giant oil refinery – representing just over 3% of the company - went on the market on Monday in Africa's biggest-ever sale of its kind.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: The minimum purchase was 10 shares for about $4 (£3) and despite this only representing a miniscule portion of the firm, many are now celebrating and joking about their new-found (part-)owner status.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: One popular social media video has a Nigerian narrating how he stopped a speeding Dangote company lorry driver, telling him not to be reckless with company property.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: Other memes show investors trying to phone up Dangote to discuss business matters.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: And the term "Yangote" – a pun in the Hausa language essentially meaning "we all have a share now" - has been trending on social media.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: On the first day of the Initial Public Offering (IPO), investment apps crashed as they could not handle the high demand.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: The Bamboo trading platform crashed as so many people tried to buy the shares Bamboo, which runs one of the most popular investor tools here, later apologised, saying: "We know we let you down." Public affairs analyst Jamil Ubah said he had rarely seen Nigerians as excited about something as this.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: He argued that it fed the dream that it could lead to greater riches for a population that is often battling to make ends meet.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: "I think the hope for the common man is that his money will grow into something big, and don't forget this is coming at a time when many are struggling as the economy is not doing great," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: Dangote wanted this to be "the people's IPO" with drivers, cooks, cleaners and servants having the chance to be part of something big.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: And they took him at his word.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: Twenty-five-year-old clothes seller Idris Lawal Musa made his first-ever stock exchange purchase and told the BBC he was happy after investing 21,000 naira ($16; £12) in 40 shares.

sentences.text: "It is no longer Dangote but 'Yangote', the company belongs to us now," he said while laughing.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: But he may make a quick sale.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: Newspaper adverts encouraged people to invest in the refinery The popularity also reflects a growing investment culture among younger Nigerians who have embraced mobile trading platforms, cryptocurrencies and digital savings products.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: But fear of missing out may have also pushed some to get into the investment business.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: But amid the frenzy, experts have warned that there are risks – shares can go down in value, as well as up, meaning people could lose some, or all, of their investment.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: Financial analyst Shuaib Uwais said prospective investors should avoid thinking of the IPO as a guaranteed route to wealth.

sentences.text: He urged people to consider a number of factors that could impact the refinery's future performance, including disruptions to crude oil supply, operational challenges, regulatory changes and fluctuations in demand for refined petroleum products.

sentences.text: "If for any reason the company experiences difficulty in sourcing its raw materials, there could be challenges," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'This is our company': Nigerians show off oil wealth after share-buying frenzy

sentences.text: Nevertheless, the IPO has given people the chance to be part of this home-grown success story.

sentences.text: Dangote's sprawling refinery on the outskirts of Lagos, which began operating two years ago and now processes around 700,000 barrels of crude a day, has transformed the fortunes of Nigeria's oil sector.

sentences.text: Until recently, Africa's largest crude oil producer had no refining capacity and had to import the finished product.

sentences.text: Now the Dangote refinery is feeding much of the domestic demand.

sentences.text: Real Madrid have won six out of seven matches in all competitions this season Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe says he stands "in full solidarity with Ceuta" after choosing to obscure a message of support for people who live in the Spanish enclave.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Real players wore T-shirts carrying the message 'Todos somos Caballas' - 'We are all Caballas' - before Tuesday's match against Elche.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Caballas is a nickname for the people of Ceuta - a Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast, bordering Morocco and separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: More than 100 people died when tens of thousands of migrants crossed into the territory from neighbouring Morocco in July.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Mbappe - along with team-mates Vinicius Jr and Ibrahima Konate - rolled up their shirts to partially cover up the message.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I want to explain this clearly so people understand," the France international said.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It was the clubs' decision to include the T-shirt and to have us wear it.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: We players had to wear it.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "The first thing I want to say is that I stand in full solidarity with Ceuta and with all the victims.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "Because before I'm a player, I'm a human being.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "But I also wanted to make a gesture and spare a thought for all the immigrants who have lost their lives and who are also living in harsh condition." Mbappe acknowledged his gesture could be misunderstood.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It wasn't an easy position to take," he said.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "It was difficult because, in the end, people might think I'm against the people of Ceuta.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I have nothing against them, and I support them 100% in my thoughts.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: But I also wanted to spare a thought for all the people who are suffering because, at the end of the day, I'm human, and I don't want to prioritise one form of suffering over another.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "There are people who are suffering, and it breaks my heart to see that happening in the world.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: I'm a young man who wants the best for the world we live in.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: "I aim to send a message of positivity and peace, and I hope this situation is resolved quickly." This video can not be played "We are all Ceutans" or not...
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Mbappe, Vinicius Jr and Konate disagree This is not the first time Real Madrid have shown support for Ceuta.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Before their Champions League meeting with Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu on 8 September, supporters in the south stand displayed cards featuring the coat of arms of the autonomous city, while the rest of the stadium joined the tribute with a round of applause.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: The initiative was part of a wider show of support for Ceuta, after at least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Most swam around a border fence and at least 100 people died during the crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Although most returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or are sleeping on the city's streets and beaches, leading to unrest there.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Locals have expressed safety concerns and some have destroyed shelters and blocked aid being supplied to the migrants.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Tuesday's pre-match gesture to show support for the territory also highlighted the differing approaches among players and clubs to the Ceuta campaign.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: Barcelona did not take part in the initiative, though players at other La Liga fixtures wore the shirts as intended.
sentences.article_title: Mbappe says he 'stands with Ceuta' after T-shirt row

sentences.text: This video can not be played How two Scots ended up playing for Uganda Teenage brothers Olly and Seb Fisher are closing in on their dream of international recognition - but it won't come from their homeland of Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Instead, the Partick Thistle duo are in line to play for Uganda.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: They believe they would become the first white players ever to represent the African nation, thanks to their mother Kate being born there.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "My gran and grandad lived out here for, I think, four or five years," Olly, 18, tells BBC Sport Scotland.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "My grandfather came out here to teach in a school then my mum was born here.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: So, it's a bit of a strange one." The siblings became aware of interest from Uganda about six months ago, following a chance conversation some time before between their father and a football consultant at a game in Nigeria.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: And, at the start of August, they were invited to attend under-20 and under-17s training camps.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: They spent last week in Jinja in the country's eastern region and will stay on for one more week, with the pair saying they're "shocked" and "honoured" at the call-ups.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "I couldn't believe it," 16-year-old striker Seb said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "It's one of those things you look at and you're shocked.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Most other people couldn't as well." Goalkeeper Olly had a similar reaction.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "A real mixture of emotions," he said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: I didn't really think that this was a possibility but I was honoured to be asked to represent Uganda.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: I thought it was a real big opportunity." Mum Kate is "ecstatic" and "thinks it'd be a great experience for us", adds Seb.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Olly Fisher, second right, with his Ugandan team-mates There is another Scottish link with Uganda, with former Hearts and Ghana midfielder Laryea Kingston currently coach of Uganda's under-20s.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: And he is the one who believes the Fisher brothers are on the verge of making history.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "Coach Kingston was saying we'd be the first white boys to play for Uganda, which would be history in the making," Seb explained.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "It is very special." And Olly added: "It's never been done before, so definitely it is very special." The pair feel like they're making connections with the African nation, having been reared on stories about Uganda from their grandparents.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: And even though they have been training in oppressively warm conditions, they are embracing the opportunity.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "Everyone has been brilliant, welcoming, really great," Seb said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "The other boys have been brand new with us.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Some of the boys actually come from the same area where my mum was born.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: So, they were all talking about that." The boys will return to Scotland soon, combining training and playing with Thistle with university and school, but are planning to rejoin their new international team-mates in the near future.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: Olly hopes to be part of his squad if they qualify for the Under-20's Africa Cup of Nations early next year, and Seb could be in the Under-17 squad for November's World Cup in Qatar.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "That's what you want as a footballer, being in an international environment," Seb said.
sentences.article_title: Meet the Scottish teenagers poised to represent Uganda

sentences.text: "It makes you a better player and hopefully it does for the two of us, and I think it will, and benefit us very much going back to Scotland playing at Thistle." The Fisher brothers with Uganda Under-20s head coach and former Hearts player Laryea Kingston

sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: But Smelyansky is no military commander.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: He is the head of Ukraine's state postal service, Ukrposhta.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: And every day he must decide how far to send his postmen and women into the deadly "kill zone" along the front lines where the threat of drone attack is ever present.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: "If it's too dangerous to go today, we won't go," Smelyansky told us.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: "We'll go tomorrow, or we'll go somewhere else.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: The key is to be as agile as you can." Ukrposhta does more than just collect letters and parcels.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: It pays out pensions in hard cash, it takes payment for utility bills.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: And it delivers vital food and medicine to people on the margins of society.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: As such, it offers a lifeline to millions of poor and elderly Ukrainians living in remote villages where shops are rare and trips to the city are expensive and dangerous.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: In a vast rural nation wracked by war, Ukrposhta is part of the glue that holds the country together.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire

sentences.text: That has made the service a target for Russia - which in recent months has stepped up not only its attacks on postmen and women but also sorting offices and logistical hubs.

sentences.text: The Kremlin has claimed strikes like this are retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian online retailers like Wildberries.
sentences.article_title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire
