sentences.text: Just last month, the European policing agency (Europol) had warned that museum thefts across Europe were growing increasingly brazen.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: And just days before the Renoir heist, internationally known art detective Arthur Brand predicted to the BBC that more high-profile burglaries were likely - particularly in the wake of the successful robbery at the Louvre in Paris last October .
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The audacious crime in one of the world's most famous museums stunned France, and the stolen jewellery worth €88m (£75m) has still not been recovered, nearly a year on.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We will see more of this," says Brand, "because if you are able to hit the Louvre, thieves all around the world are watching that, thinking, 'Wow' - and then they think, 'Don't we have a local museum with gold and silver?'".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: This video can not be played What we know about the Renoir museum heist Within hours of the Louvre burglary, thieves had raided coins from a smaller museum in France.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Since then, criminals have stolen a diamond necklace in Vienna , Bronze Age artefacts in Spain , and art from two Italian museums - and that's only what the BBC has written about.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The heist at the Renoir Museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer is the latest, and detectives are still working to track down the remaining multi-million-pound paintings - two of which were quickly recovered after thieves dropped them in the museum garden.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Europol tells the BBC the number of museum theft cases reported to them across Europe began to increase about two years ago.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Its recent report says both the methods and targets of thefts are changing - with a rise in more forceful tactics, and, as in the Louvre case, a focus on high-value items such as precious metals and gemstones.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Both Brand and Ibrahim Bulut, a museum security expert from a Belgian security consulting firm, believe many thefts that followed the Louvre burglary are copycats.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Every museum in the world is stressing now," Brand says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Data provided to the BBC by ARCA shows recorded museum thefts in France spiked in 2024, and rose again slightly in 2025.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, numbers go up and down over time, with more thefts recorded in 2015 than a decade later.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Others point out the colonial history behind many treasures in European museums, with art historians highlighting the French crown jewels stolen from the Louvre contained emeralds, diamonds, sapphires and pearls which are not native to France.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are vulnerable and easy to burgle, Brand says, compared with well-secured jewellery shops and banks - which these days hold less cash.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Directors historically "never have enough money for security" or prefer to spend it on the next exhibition, and museums are often housed in old buildings that are difficult to protect, he adds.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: For example, the Denis Diderot Maison des Lumières (House of Enlightenment) - burgled hours after the Louvre - is housed in two 18th-Century mansions in Langres.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We therefore have to reconcile modern security requirements with the need to preserve historic buildings and comply with France's heritage regulations," local mayor Théo Caviezel explains.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are also open public spaces that have less access control and perpetrators can come in as visitors, says Kumar Sokka, CEO of Acre Security which works with some museums in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: And even if a museum is secured well, thieves could still come in armed, Brand says, adding that it would be impractical to put police in galleries.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Many of these burglaries are over in minutes and the thieves have long gone by the time police show up - the Renoir case happened within five minutes.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Heists used to depend on deception, but burglaries are now becoming increasingly violent, Europol's report last month , external points out.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Offenders are using tools such as sledgehammers, axes, crowbars and, in some instances, explosives, to get inside.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In the Louvre, the thieves used a mechanical lift to gain access, cut through the window with power tools and then threatened guards, who left, before forcing their way inside displays and grabbing the jewels.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In the Renoir case, the perpetrators used an electric knife to cut through a fence before sawing through structures holding the paintings' frames in place.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The increased aggression creates new security concerns.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "An armed incident during opening hours, like the one we experienced, creates a situation in which the immediate priority is to keep our audience and staff safe," says Lilli Hollein, the director of the Museum of Applied Arts (MAK) in Vienna, which was burgled last month.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: Two people leave Louvre in lift mounted to vehicle What is being stolen is also changing.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: While paintings are still taken, they're harder to sell, so about 10 years ago, thieves began shifting to goods that are easier to get rid of, Brand says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Now precious metals, gemstones, and culturally significant artefacts including Chinese porcelain are increasingly targeted, according to Europol's report.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Precious metals can be easily melted down, leaving no trace for law enforcement, and facilitating illicit sales during the fencing process," it says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Precious stones in jewellery, on the other hand, can be easily removed and sold further." Meanwhile, Chinese porcelain is likely to be easily sold on the art market because of high demand, Europol says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: After a theft, police generally have between four and six days to catch the thieves, according to Brand, who works with investigators by calling informants and receiving tips from the public or even ex-partners of perpetrators.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: But while suspects may be arrested, jewels or precious metals might not be found - such as with the Louvre case.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: On the other hand, Brand believes the Renoir paintings stolen this week - two of which were dropped by the thieves on their way out - "will probably be recovered" because "no one will want to buy" them and "it is likely, then, that the thieves have no idea what to do with them".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Christopher A Marinello, the boss of Art Recovery International that recovers stolen art, says only 5-10% of stolen art is ever recovered, making thefts from small museums like this week's "extra painful".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Tuesday's heist is another example of "Europe's museums under siege", he adds.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: After its theft in October, Maison des Lumières launched a security audit carried out by police officers appointed by France's cultural ministry, mayor Caviezel says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Some recommendations are already being implemented, such as enhanced video surveillance, while other structural improvements are in the process of being developed.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: MAK in Vienna also increased its security to prevent "copycat offenders and to provide our audience with visible security", its director says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Entry is through a metal detector, and bags must be put in the cloakroom or in lockers, and there are more security guards.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Experts say the trick is to create physical barriers that will delay thieves so there is time for the police to arrive, or to make any theft take so long that it would deter would-be offenders from attempting it.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "Security is about buying time", says Bulut.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Sokka says it's critical to have integrated systems - so for example if an alarm goes off, you could shut down the facility, or lock down all high net worth paintings.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, security measures are expensive.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Mayor Caviezel, whose small French city hosts two museums and collections, says finding the money is "one of our main challenges".
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "A small city can be entrusted with collections of national importance without having the financial resources of a major Parisian institution." Bulut, who sits on the International Committee for Museum Security board, says it's not all about expensive gadgets.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: It could also be training guards to spot suspicious people who may be casing a museum and ask them if they need help, which may deter them from returning.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museums are investing: Sokka says his company has seen an uptick in seismic offerings, that can detect vibration such as drilling in walls, in the past 18 months.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: Museum heists are not increasing everywhere in Europe.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: In Sweden, major museum thefts began to decline around a decade ago and have not changed significantly in recent years, said Peg Magnusson, Sweden's representative for a Unesco convention to combat illicit trafficking of cultural property.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: However, other worrying cultural artefact targets have emerged.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: The challenge for museums now is increasing security while also staying open to the public.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "A museum cannot be a fortress," Hollein says.
sentences.article_title: Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe

sentences.text: "We want to be open institutions; at the same time, we are facing new challenges and attacks against museums that will require new standards." Additional reporting by Madeleine Lake.
